title: A Streaming Collectives Interface Targeting Dataflow Acceleration and HPC Workloads
problem: Dataflow accelerators lack scalable collective communication support; no framework for accelerator-initiated MPI
motivation: Dataflow accelerators offer energy efficiency but limited by communication capabilities; HLS interface needed for HPC adoption
method: They built a streaming interface—continuous data pipelines created through hardware synthesis tools—that enables communication between a host computer and a dataflow accelerator (a processor optimized for routing data through operations). The interface uses MPI (the standard multi-computer communication protocol) and allows the accelerator itself to initiate collective operations, which are coordinated data exchanges involving multiple processors. They validated the design using an enhanced version of the HPL benchmark from the HPCC_FPGA suite.
key_novelty: A collective communication interface using data streaming for dataflow accelerators that reduces hardware resource consumption.
contributions: Superlinear speedup in strong scaling stencil benchmark
limitations: Evaluation limited to 16 FPGAs; specific to HPL and stencil workloads
